- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the mid-to-late period of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to lag behind true values, particularly after sharp upward spikes in the history.
- Overshoots occur after recent spikes, where model predicts a peak and then drops too quickly.
- Mean reversion is overestimated — model assumes prices return to prior levels too fast, missing sustained upward trends.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the early part of the horizon, underreacting to recent volatility.
- Model fails to capture the full magnitude of upward momentum in the last 5–10 days of history.
- Overly smooth forecasts ignore recent volatility clustering; model treats sharp moves as temporary noise.
- Forecasts often underestimate the persistence of upward trends, especially when history shows strong momentum.
- Model tends to overcorrect downward moves, predicting a quick recovery instead of a sustained dip.
- Forecasts are too sensitive to recent low values, leading to premature overcorrection or underestimation of rebound.
